## `packages/zig_runtime/README.md`

<!-- eyg-source: {"path":"packages/zig_runtime/README.md","sha256":"7621dc19ea98b9718bf5558f8668d5135a5c95d3cf3e7e46c3c72cb7dceff2fd","bytes":4587} -->
````text
# EYG in Zig

A native interpreter and structural terminal shell, tested against the actual
Gleam implementation on `next-tui`. The executable starts the TUI when run
without arguments, as `gleam run -- tui` does.

The oracle is pinned to `be502aa03df926a8f9df474a0a7fe16c8fb14fbd`.
The Git reference is `real-world` at
`f1e32bad77d7ffdef6c416cb7ccbf7b23ec0bbd9`.
Neither oracle checkout is changed by the test adapters.

## Build and use

Use Zig **0.14.1**. The wrapper uses an installed compiler or installs the
versioned `ziglang` package into this package's ignored `work/` directory.

```sh
cd packages/zig_runtime
./scripts/zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast
./zig-out/bin/eyg
./zig-out/bin/eyg eval -c '!int_add(20, 22)'
./scripts/zig build test
```

The TUI requires terminal input and output. Ctrl+Q exits; bracketed paste
inserts a program; Enter executes it. Arrow keys navigate; `n` inserts an
integer, `s` a string, `j` a builtin, and `q` a file import. The displayed
selection and type information follow the pinned oracle.

The interpreter uses canonical EYG DAG-JSON IR. The source parser, lexical
closures, curried primitives, delimited multi-shot effect continuations,
Unicode grapheme operations and type/effect inference are native Zig.
The runtime uses Zig's standard library for compression, hashes, Ed25519,
HTTP/TLS, allocation and terminal I/O. No Gleam, JavaScript, Git subprocess or
OpenSSL dependency is needed to run the desktop binary.

## Reproduce the oracle checks

Development tests additionally require Git, Gleam 1.19.2, Bun, and Python 3.
For terminal tests, install the pinned test dependencies in `tests/requirements.txt`.

```sh
./scripts/prepare-oracles.sh
python3 -m pip install --target ../../work/test-dependencies -r tests/requirements.txt
python3 tests/differential.py --programs 5000 --syntax 1000 --traces 100
python3 tests/differential_input.py --cases 1000
python3 tests/pty_parity.py --help
python3 tests/differential_inference.py --help
python3 tests/differential_computer.py --help
```

`reports/` contains machine-readable measurements and counterexamples. A
mismatch is a failed gate. Every generated trace compares the initial buffer
and the buffer after **every** event, including symbol, display width,
foreground/background, modifiers, underline color and link. Failing traces
are reduced and saved with their seed. Replay one with
`tests/differential.py --replay reports/failures/<file>.json`.

The JSONL adapter is `eyg --protocol`. It provides `eval`, `parse`, `diagnostic`,
`input`, `tui`, `bench_tui` and `git` operations. This adapter exposes the native
implementations; it does not invoke the oracle.

## Performance

```sh
python3 tests/benchmark.py --iterations 100 --oracle
```

The benchmark reports p50/p95/p99/maximum and fails if any measured native
dispatch-plus-frame sample reaches 10 ms. Its correctness gate must refer to
the same executable hash and a complete passing differential campaign. Real
PTY tests separately measure key-to-ANSI-frame time, including transport.
An isolated Escape deliberately waits for the oracle's 40 ms escape-sequence
ambiguity timer; that physical-key latency cannot meet a universal 10 ms goal.

Native Git effects run on a worker thread in the TUI, with a running indicator,
completion resumption and cancellation of waiting. Initial feedback and final
query completion are separate measurements. Large results still take time to
convert and render; filesystem durability and OS scheduling can produce tail
latencies. Saved reports retain outliers.

## Git, Android, book and talk

- [Git API and verification](git/README.md): native objects, packs/deltas,
  filtered history, remotes, trees, commits and compare-and-swap refs.
- [Android app](android/README.md): shared Zig interpreter through JNI and an
  Expo phone-effects host. The APK build currently needs the environment to
  allow `repo.reactnative.dev`, which hosts React Native's Android artifact.
- [Crafting an EYG interpreter](docs/book.md): concise chapters for experienced
  programmers new to Zig, library decisions and implementation reviews.
- [Complete source listings](docs/source-listings.md): hash-checked files from
  which the real runtime can be extracted and built.
- [Talk](docs/talk.md): oracle design, generated programs and interactions,
  counterexample reduction, native acceleration and performance evidence.

Use `docs/book_sources.py --help` to regenerate or reconstruct the source
appendix. A source reconstruction is separately built and tested; it is not
merely illustrative pseudocode.
````

## `packages/zig_runtime/android/App.tsx`

<!-- eyg-source: {"path":"packages/zig_runtime/android/App.tsx","sha256":"703451c564d0f1f89539ec06e7884b448c14016cfa0ee177e95c0e7f30b1e955","bytes":6313} -->
```tsx
import React, { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { Alert, Button, ScrollView, StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, View } from 'react-native';
import { SafeAreaProvider, SafeAreaView } from 'react-native-safe-area-context';
import { requireNativeModule } from 'expo-modules-core';
import { Paths } from 'expo-file-system';
import { expoModules } from './src/modules';
import { backgroundReady } from './src/background-bootstrap';
// The effect boundary is ordinary JS so node can test it without native mocks.
// @ts-ignore
import { ExpoEffects } from './src/effects.mjs';
// @ts-ignore
import { runSession } from './src/session.mjs';
// @ts-ignore
import { renderView } from './src/views.mjs';

type NativeRuntime = {
  pureSync(request: string): string;
  create(): Promise<number>;
  evaluate(id: number, request: string): Promise<string>;
  resume(id: number, reply: string): Promise<string>;
  destroy(id: number): Promise<void>;
};
type ViewSpec = { id: string; module: string; component: string; props?: Record<string, unknown>; children?: unknown; ref?: boolean | string };
type RunContext = { controller: AbortController; host: ExpoEffects | null };
type NativeView = { owner: RunContext; child: React.ReactNode };

const initialProgram = `let result = perform Expo({
  module: "expo-battery",
  method: "getBatteryLevelAsync",
  args: []
})
result`;

function Workspace() {
  const [source, setSource] = useState(initialProgram);
  const [output, setOutput] = useState('Ready. Run EYG to evaluate with the Zig interpreter.');
  const [running, setRunning] = useState(false);
  const [views, setViews] = useState<Record<string, NativeView>>({});
  const activeRun = useRef<RunContext | null>(null);
  const mounted = useRef(true);
  useEffect(() => {
    mounted.current = true;
    return () => {
      mounted.current = false;
      const context = activeRun.current;
      activeRun.current = null;
      context?.controller.abort();
      context?.host?.close().catch(() => {});
    };
  }, []);

  function cancel() {
    const context = activeRun.current;
    if (!context) return;
    activeRun.current = null;
    context.controller.abort();
    context.host?.close().catch(() => {});
    setViews({});
    setOutput('Cancelled.');
    setRunning(false);
  }

  async function run() {
    if (activeRun.current) return;
    const context: RunContext = { controller: new AbortController(), host: null };
    activeRun.current = context;
    const current = () => mounted.current && activeRun.current === context && !context.controller.signal.aborted;
    setRunning(true);
    const host = new ExpoEffects(expoModules, {
      show: (spec: ViewSpec, emit: (topic: string, args: unknown[]) => void) => {
        if (!current()) throw new Error('Closed EYG run');
        if (!spec.id) throw new Error('Missing native view id');
        const child = renderView(spec, host, React.createElement, { rootStyle: styles.nativeView, emit, current });
        setViews(previous => current() ? { ...previous, [spec.id]: { owner: context, child } } : previous);
        return spec.id;
      },
      close: (id: string) => {
        if (mounted.current) setViews(previous => {
          if (previous[id]?.owner !== context) return previous;
          const next = { ...previous };
          delete next[id];
          return next;
        });
        return null;
      },
      clear: () => {
        if (mounted.current) setViews(previous => Object.fromEntries(
          Object.entries(previous).filter(([, view]) => view.owner !== context),
        ));
      },
    }, 1024, { pure: (request: string) => requireNativeModule<NativeRuntime>('EygRuntime').pureSync(request) });
    context.host = host;
    try {
      await backgroundReady;
      const native = requireNativeModule<NativeRuntime>('EygRuntime');
      const response = await runSession(native, host, source, (state: {label: string}) => { if (current()) setOutput(`Waiting for ${state.label}…`); }, undefined, { directory: Paths.document.uri }, context.controller.signal);
      if (current()) setOutput(JSON.stringify(response, null, 2));
    } catch (error) {
      if (current()) setOutput(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
    } finally {
      host.close().catch(() => {});
      if (activeRun.current === context) {
        activeRun.current = null;
        if (mounted.current) setRunning(false);
      }
    }
  }

  return <SafeAreaView style={styles.root}>
    <Text style={styles.title}>EYG · native Zig</Text>
    <Text style={styles.hint}>Phone APIs are explicit effects. Android permission prompts belong to the called Expo API.</Text>
    <TextInput accessibilityLabel="EYG program" multiline autoCapitalize="none" autoCorrect={false} value={source} onChangeText={setSource} editable={!running} style={styles.editor} />
    <View style={styles.actions}>
      <Button title={running ? 'Running…' : 'Run'} onPress={run} disabled={running} />
      <Button title="Cancel" disabled={!running} onPress={cancel} />
      <Button title="Effects" onPress={() => Alert.alert('Expo effects', 'Expo calls SDK methods; ExpoView mounts native components; ExpoNextEvent receives callbacks; ExpoReply answers async callbacks; ExpoRelease closes a native object. Use defer for SDK operations waiting for a callback. Call requestPermissionsAsync explicitly before protected APIs.')} />
    </View>
    {Object.entries(views).map(([id, view]) => <View key={id}>{view.child}</View>)}
    <ScrollView style={styles.output}><Text selectable style={styles.result}>{output}</Text></ScrollView>
  </SafeAreaView>;
}

export default function App() { return <SafeAreaProvider><Workspace /></SafeAreaProvider>; }
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  root: { flex: 1, backgroundColor: '#101818', padding: 16 },
  title: { color: '#cef1ca', fontSize: 24, fontWeight: '600', marginBottom: 8 },
  hint: { color: '#a2b8ad', marginBottom: 12 },
  editor: { color: '#eaf5eb', backgroundColor: '#1b2924', borderRadius: 8, padding: 12, fontFamily: 'monospace', minHeight: 230, textAlignVertical: 'top' },
  actions: { flexDirection: 'row', justifyContent: 'space-around', marginVertical: 12 },
  output: { flex: 1 }, result: { color: '#eaf5eb', fontFamily: 'monospace' },
  nativeView: { width: '100%', height: 240 },
});
```

## `packages/zig_runtime/android/README.md`

<!-- eyg-source: {"path":"packages/zig_runtime/android/README.md","sha256":"e7278f581aa66155a7cb94c980abd5feef37e10b4f739b43abb333e9d0961bb4","bytes":19547} -->
````text
# EYG on Android

The app runs the same Zig evaluator as the terminal binary. An Expo module calls
a small JNI shim; each native session owns an arena and an explicit interpreter
continuation. Evaluation runs on Kotlin's IO dispatcher. A suspended phone effect
returns to JavaScript, awaits the real Expo API, then resumes Zig with `Ok(value)`
or `Error(message)`. The UI thread does not wait for native evaluation.

## Build

Use Node 24, Java 21 for Gradle, a Java 17 compile toolchain, Zig 0.14.1 and the Android SDK/NDK. Dependencies and exact
versions are recorded in `package-lock.json`; SDK 58 currently uses Android 37,
build tools 37.0.0 and NDK 27.1.12297006.

```sh
cd packages/zig_runtime/android
npm ci
npm test
npm run typecheck
npm run check:capabilities
EXPO_NO_TELEMETRY=1 npm run prebuild -- --no-install
ZIG=/path/to/zig ANDROID_NDK_HOME=/path/to/ndk ./build-runtime.sh
ANDROID_HOME=/path/to/sdk npm run android
```

`build-runtime.sh` builds ARM64 and x86-64 Zig/JNI libraries with 16 KiB page
alignment. Build the native libraries after a clean checkout; they are generated
files and are not committed. `npm run android` needs a connected device or
emulator. Expo Go cannot load this custom native module.

The managed build in this delivery reached Android/Kotlin compilation but could
not assemble an APK: Maven Central redirects React Native's Android artifact to
the following host, which the environment's network policy denied with HTTP 403:

```text
https://repo.reactnative.dev/maven2/com/facebook/react/react-android/0.88.1/react-android-0.88.1-debug.aar
```

Allow `repo.reactnative.dev` in the environment network configuration, then rerun
the Gradle build. No APK or device launch is claimed. Android ARM64 and x86-64
Zig/JNI shared libraries were successfully cross-compiled before this blocker.
`apk-build-blocker.txt` and `validation.json` preserve the observed status.

The installed React Native package also documents a supported source composite
build. An isolated offline attempt substituted ReactAndroid and Hermes projects
under `work/source-build`; it stopped before task graph creation because the
Kotlin 2.2.0 Gradle plugin marker was not cached. Full native third-party sources
are also absent from the npm package. Its normal Boost publisher,
`archives.boost.io`, is outside this environment's enforced allowed hosts, so no
source download or alternate source URL was attempted. Exact upstream source
URLs, local prerequisites and the offline command are recorded in
`source-build-feasibility.json`. The validated app and native artifacts were
preserved throughout this isolated check.

## Phone effects

These effects are necessary because the CLI host has no camera, sensors, or
Android lifecycle. Their shared protocol exposes general host capabilities
instead of introducing a separate effect for each Expo method.

| Effect | Payload | Result inside `Ok` |
|---|---|---|
| `Expo` | `{module, method, args}` | Awaited SDK result |
| `Expo` | `{expo_handle, method, args}` | A native object's method result |
| `Expo` | `{module, method, args, defer: True({})}` | Handle for an operation still running |
| `Expo` | `{expo_handle, method: "$await"}` | Awaited result; consumes the deferred handle |
| `Expo` | `{object, method, get: True({})}` | Property from foreign data; method can be a path list |
| `Expo` | `{module, method, get: True({})}` | SDK constant/property |
| `Expo` | `{module, method, construct: True({}), args}` | Constructed SDK object handle |
| `ExpoView` | `{id, module, component, props, children, ref}` | View ID; mount/update an exported component tree |
| `ExpoView` | `{id, action: "close"}` | Empty result |
| `ExpoNextEvent` | `{timeout_ms}` | Next callback event, or `None({})` |
| `ExpoReply` | `{token, value}` or `{token, error}` | Resolve/reject an async SDK callback |
| `ExpoRelease` | `{expo_handle}` | Empty result; remove/release/close native object |
| `GitQuery` | Native Git request record | Native local Git result; shared with the desktop runtime |

`Expo({method: "$modules"})` lists the registered modules.
`Expo({module: "expo-camera", method: "$members"})` lists available members.
The registry includes 67 Expo feature packages, React Native, and bundled Android
libraries for storage, payments, graphics, native controls, WebView and gestures.
It exposes 101 package entrypoints plus `eyg-widgets` and `eyg-background`. The complete
SDK58 bundled manifest has 124 entries: 90 registered dependency packages and
34 explicit exclusions, with no unclassified entries. `capabilities.json` records
installed versions, decisions, evidence paths and platform/configuration limits.
Registration does not establish that every export or hardware feature works.
React hooks remain React hooks; call imperative SDK functions or mount components.

```eyg
let permissions = perform Expo({
  module: "expo-location", method: "requestForegroundPermissionsAsync", args: []
})
match permissions {
  Ok(permission) -> {
    match permission.granted {
      True(_) -> {
        perform Expo({
          module: "expo-location", method: "getCurrentPositionAsync", args: [{}]
        })
      }
      False(_) -> { Error("Location permission denied") }
    }
  }
  Error(message) -> { Error(message) }
}
```

Permission request methods must be called explicitly. Expo and Android retain
responsibility for permission checks. Unsupported hardware, denied permissions,
missing provider configuration, and unavailable APIs produce `Error` replies.

The value boundary preserves data without adding floating point to EYG:

- Native objects are `{expo_handle: integer}`. Pass the integer as `expo_handle` for
  subsequent method calls, or the whole record inside `args`.
- `{expo_callback: "topic"}` arguments become callbacks. `ExpoNextEvent` returns
  `{topic, args, dropped}`. The queue holds 1,024 events; `dropped` reports overflow.
- Add `expo_return: value` to return declared data synchronously from a callback.
  Add `expo_reply: True({})` instead to return a promise and receive a
  `callback_token` in its event; answer with `ExpoReply({token, value})` or reject
  with `ExpoReply({token, error})`. `expo_timeout_ms` bounds that callback's wait
  (default 30,000 ms; maximum 300,000 ms). These modes cannot be combined.
- When an SDK call waits for its callback, use `defer: True({})`. Receive the
  event, answer its callback token, then call `Expo({expo_handle, method: "$await"})`.
  This lets the EYG program make the callback decision before awaiting the
  original operation.
- Add `expo_sync: "(args) -> { ... }"` for an argument-dependent synchronous EYG
  decision. It receives a list of callback arguments and returns ordinary data.
  This runs an isolated native VM, with no effects, references or captured live
  continuation. `expo_steps` defaults to 1,000 and has a maximum of 10,000 total
  definition-plus-call steps. Limits are 4 MiB allocator capacity, 4,096 source
  bytes, 64 KiB request/output and bounded argument depth/size. `!equal`,
  `!string_split`, `!string_split_once` and `!string_replace` are rejected because
  their recursive/search work runs outside the VM step loop. Scalar comparison,
  string predicates and tag matching remain available. Budget/exhaustion errors
  throw synchronously to the calling SDK. Return modes cannot be combined.
  Source may also be canonical DAG-JSON IR text; use a Select node to read SDK
  fields such as `canAskAgain` that surface EYG identifiers cannot spell.
- Fractional and unsafe integers are `{expo_number: "51.5072"}`. Passing this
  record in `args` restores the JavaScript number, preserving coordinates,
  brightness, battery levels, and sensor readings.
- Typed bytes use `{expo_bytes: [0, 255]}`. Native EYG binary effect payloads are
  also decoded to this byte representation.
- Dates use `{expo_date: "2026-10-28T12:00:00.000Z"}`. Passing the wrapper in
  arguments restores a JavaScript Date; SDK Date results preserve the same value.
- `None({})` crosses to JavaScript `null`; `True({})` and `False({})` become booleans.

EYG field names use lowercase letters and underscores; `handle` is reserved.
The protocol therefore uses `expo_handle` and `timeout_ms`. Existing JavaScript
clients can still use `handle` and `timeoutMs`.
For SDK option names such as `shouldShowBanner`, construct a dictionary with
`{expo_object: [{key: "shouldShowBanner", value: True({})}]}`. Read foreign data
with `Expo({object: data, method: "canAskAgain", get: True({})})`. A method path
list such as `["metadata", "a.b"]` addresses a literal key containing a dot.

An ExpoView with `ref: True({})` emits `view:<id>:ready` with the object handle.
Use that handle for camera capture and similar component methods. Use the same
view ID to update its props. Event handler props accept `expo_callback` records.
Refs are opt-in because many functional UI components do not accept a ref.
The `children` field accepts text and nested `{module, component, props, children}`
descriptors; nested refs may use a string event topic. This permits Compose
Host/Column layouts, provider components and other native component composition.
Trees are limited to 64 levels and reject cycles.
Views belong to the current run: await `ExpoNextEvent` while they are in use;
returning from the program closes its owned view surface.

SDK58 widgets, Material Symbols and Advertising ID have Android support, even
though some package READMEs/native metadata emphasize iOS. `@expo/ui` also exposes
its Jetpack Compose, modifiers and Android community-adapter entrypoints.
`expo-updates` is registered, but remote updates require an updates URL, runtime
configuration and a release build. No remote update service is configured here.

`Expo({module: "eyg-widgets", method: "home", args: [{text: "42 commits"}]})`
returns the declared `EygWidget` provider's object handle. Call its
`updateSnapshot` with `{tree: {component: "Text", children: "Query complete"}}`.
Its precompiled layout accepts nested Text/Column/Row/Box/Image/Icon/Button,
Spacer/Divider/Checkbox/Switch/Card and progress-indicator descriptors with
ordinary JSON props. `notification` returns an Expo custom-notification factory;
call `post` with `{sections: {collapsed: tree, expanded: tree}}` and SDK options.
Updates use the same `{sections: ...}` shape. Permissions still use the normal
notification API. The actual Expo widget compiler is tested; posting and home
screen rendering still require an Android device. Additional widget provider
names and custom native layouts require a rebuild. Widget/Worklets callbacks
cannot capture a runtime EYG continuation; background continuation persistence
is not implemented.

## Durable background entrypoints

`eyg-background` saves EYG task source and JSON metadata in AsyncStorage. Sixteen
TaskManager dispatchers are defined synchronously at bundle initialization;
incoming cold-start events wait for durable definitions to restore. Each event
starts a fresh native session with `input` bound to
`{data, error, execution_info, metadata}`. It can perform ordinary phone/native
effects and retains its result after the JavaScript process exits.

Call `Expo({module: "eyg-background", method: "define", args: [{name: "history",
source: "input.data", result_kind: "task"}]})`. The result's `task_name` is the
stable OS slot name. Register that name through `expo-background-task`,
`expo-location` or another normal Expo scheduling API. Defining source does not
schedule OS work or grant permissions. `result_kind` selects BackgroundTask
(`task`), BackgroundFetch (`fetch`) or raw callback data (`value`) results.

`list`, `get(name)` and `result(name)` inspect saved definitions/results;
`run(name, data)` starts an immediate fresh invocation. `cancel(name)` aborts
an active invocation. `forget(name)` cancels it, unregisters its OS task and
removes its definition/result. Sources are limited to 64 KiB, metadata to 16 KiB,
callback input to 512 KiB and stored result values to 64 KiB. Timeouts default
to 30 seconds, configurable from 1 ms to 300 seconds; Android may impose a
shorter lifetime. Native operations already in progress may finish after cancel,
while the session's sticky cancellation prevents later effects.

Slot/name identities remain reserved after `forget` so delayed OS events cannot
reach a different task. There are at most sixteen historical names. To reclaim
them, forget all definitions and call `resetSlots`; it verifies that no reserved
OS tasks remain, closes the adapter and returns `{restart_required: True({})}`.
Restart the JavaScript process before defining new names. This persistence
stores entrypoint source, not a suspended interpreter continuation. Actual OS
scheduling, restart delivery and battery restrictions require device validation.

`Fetch`, `EYGParse`, `DecodeJSON`, `CreateKey`, `Sign`, `Hash`, and `Inflate` also
use the shared native implementations and the existing CLI effect contracts.
TLS remains verified; Android trusts hashed PEM/DER certificate files from both
`/apex/com.android.conscrypt/cacerts` and `/system/etc/security/cacerts`.

`GitQuery` executes the shared Zig object/pack/index/delta/query implementation
on the native IO dispatcher. A repository must be accessible in the app's Android
sandbox; for example, use Expo FileSystem to place a repository in its document
directory, then evaluate `perform GitQuery({action: "history", repo: "repo", limit: 20})`.
The app sends its document directory as the native session's working directory.
The native request API also accepts an explicit `directory` path or `file://` URI.

Relative `import "module.eyg"` and `.eyg.json` imports are read natively.
Initialization is pure, matching the Gleam oracle. Returned functions retain
their source directory and can perform phone/native effects when invoked by
the caller. Cycles and imports deeper than 64 modules fail explicitly.

Named packages, explicit versions, pinned releases, and content references use
the shared EYG hub cache. It verifies every module's CID against its canonical
bytes before evaluation. Module initialization is pure and requires pinned
dependencies; returned functions run under the caller's normal phone/native
effect handler. The default origin is `https://eyg.run`; `EYG_ORIGIN` or the C ABI
request's `hubOrigin` can configure another origin.

Tests can supply a `packages` fixture object in the native evaluation request.
Fixtures go through the same canonical hash validation and disable live hub
downloads, so missing-package and invalid-CID tests are reproducible.

Closing/cancelling a run removes subscriptions, closes owned objects, clears
views, resolves event waits, and destroys the native arena. A resource returned
after cancellation is disposed as soon as its pending API call completes.
Cancellation does not revoke an OS operation that the underlying Expo API cannot
cancel. Zig's instruction budget bounds runaway EYG programs.
The Kotlin owner retains an active native session until its IO worker finishes.
Closing the app drops ownership without waiting for an in-flight hub/HTTP read;
the last worker releases the arena after the operation returns.
Cancel re-enables editing immediately and isolates a newer run from old results
and view cleanup. It also sets a sticky atomic native cancellation flag. The
current OS operation can finish; checks after IO and before later effects prevent
the interpreter from continuing to another native mutation. The JNI owner signals
cancellation under its ownership lock and frees the pointer only after its last
active call returns.

## Oracle checks

The ordinary JS tests include 2,000 seeded value-boundary cases and lifecycle
checks for subscriptions, denied permissions, native object identity, view
ownership, cancellation, and late API results.

The C ABI can be tested without an Android emulator. This exercises the real Zig
interpreter, session allocation, effect suspension, continuation resume, parser,
UTF-8/JSON bytes, and invalid-reply checks:

```sh
cd packages/zig_runtime
mkdir -p android/work
zig build-lib src/android_bridge.zig -dynamic -lc -O ReleaseFast \
  --name eyg_android_host \
  -femit-bin=android/work/libeyg_android_host.so
python3 android/scripts/test-native.py android/work/libeyg_android_host.so \
  --cases 1000 --oracle --bun bun
```

Prepare the pinned `next-tui` oracle first with `scripts/prepare-oracles.sh`.
`--oracle` compares 1,000 generated programs and 1,000 suspended-effect programs
against the actual Gleam interpreter through the Android C ABI. The generator
uses seed `0x455947`; failure output retains the program and both results.
`python3 android/scripts/test-jni.py --zig zig --jdk /path/to/jdk` also compiles
and runs the actual JNI C shim on a Linux JDK, including 1,000 suspend/resume
calls and UTF-8/embedded-NUL byte round trips.
`python3 android/scripts/test-lifecycle.py --jdk /path/to/jdk` compiles the actual
Kotlin session owner and checks concurrent close/destroy/queued-call schedules
without Android mocks. Use `--gradle-cache /path/to/gradle-user-home` if its cached
Kotlin compiler jars are outside the default Gradle cache. The native suite also covers all hub reference forms,
CID mismatch rejection, pure initialization, native Fetch against a loopback
server, parser/decoder/hash/inflate wiring, and the RFC 8032 Ed25519 test vector.
From the Android directory, `node tests/phone-flow.mjs` runs generated EYG
programs through the real C ABI, production effect dispatcher, and deterministic
SDK fixture. It checks deferred callbacks, replies, foreign field names,
cancellation, and complete ownership cleanup. This is host integration testing;
it does not stand in for device validation.
From `packages/zig_runtime`,
`python3 android/scripts/test-cancel.py android/work/libeyg_android_host.so`
checks a real blocked native HTTP request followed by a Git repository creation.
The positive control creates the repository; cancelling the blocked run prevents
the subsequent mutation and keeps that session cancelled.
`node tests/sync-flow.mjs` exercises argument-dependent callbacks through the
real bounded native evaluator, including forbidden operations and clean memory,
output and step exhaustion. `scripts/test-sync-jni.py` verifies its actual
synchronous JNI entrypoint. `node tests/background-flow.mjs` restarts three real
native processes, restores durable definitions/results, delivers a cold event
before hydration completes, and checks input, cancellation and resource cleanup.

## Verification limits

`validation.json` records the checks actually run. A compiled library, successful
Metro bundle, and host oracle parity do not establish that every phone API works
on real hardware. Device permission flows, camera/media capture, sensors, maps,
notifications, and OS lifecycle/background behavior require device validation.
Durable background source entrypoints restart fresh VMs; serializing an existing
EYG continuation is not implemented. Maps needs a
provider API key; push notifications need project/provider configuration.
Native hub, HTTP, relative filesystem imports, and local Git are implemented and
tested through the host C ABI. Android certificate-directory selection is
cross-compiled; live Android TLS and OS behavior still require device validation.

The Android editor is a native mobile source editor and result view. Terminal
cell rendering remains covered by the desktop TUI oracle suite; no Android
pixel-equivalence claim is made for this different interface.
````

```text
apply plugin: "com.android.application"
apply plugin: "org.jetbrains.kotlin.android"
apply plugin: "com.facebook.react"

def projectRoot = rootDir.getAbsoluteFile().getParentFile().getAbsolutePath()

/**
 * This is the configuration block to customize your React Native Android app.
 * By default you don't need to apply any configuration, just uncomment the lines you need.
 */
react {
    entryFile = file(["node", "-e", "require('expo/scripts/resolveAppEntry')", projectRoot, "android", "absolute"].execute(null, rootDir).text.trim())
    reactNativeDir = new File(["node", "--print", "require.resolve('react-native/package.json')"].execute(null, rootDir).text.trim()).getParentFile().getAbsoluteFile()
    hermesCommand = new File(["node", "--print", "require.resolve('hermes-compiler/package.json', { paths: [require.resolve('react-native/package.json')] })"].execute(null, rootDir).text.trim()).getParentFile().getAbsolutePath() + "/hermesc/%OS-BIN%/hermesc"
    codegenDir = new File(["node", "--print", "require.resolve('@react-native/codegen/package.json', { paths: [require.resolve('react-native/package.json')] })"].execute(null, rootDir).text.trim()).getParentFile().getAbsoluteFile()

    enableBundleCompression = (findProperty('android.enableBundleCompression') ?: false).toBoolean()
    // Use Expo CLI to bundle the app, this ensures the Metro config
    // works correctly with Expo projects.
    cliFile = new File(["node", "--print", "require.resolve('@expo/cli', { paths: [require.resolve('expo/package.json')] })"].execute(null, rootDir).text.trim())
    bundleCommand = "export:embed"

    /* Folders */
     //   The root of your project, i.e. where "package.json" lives. Default is '../..'
    // root = file("../../")
    //   The folder where the react-native NPM package is. Default is ../../node_modules/react-native
    // reactNativeDir = file("../../node_modules/react-native")
    //   The folder where the react-native Codegen package is. Default is ../../node_modules/@react-native/codegen
    // codegenDir = file("../../node_modules/@react-native/codegen")

    /* Variants */
    //   The list of variants to that are debuggable. For those we're going to
    //   skip the bundling of the JS bundle and the assets. By default is just 'debug'.
    //   If you add flavors like lite, prod, etc. you'll have to list your debuggableVariants.
    // debuggableVariants = ["liteDebug", "prodDebug"]

    /* Bundling */
    //   A list containing the node command and its flags. Default is just 'node'.
    // nodeExecutableAndArgs = ["node"]

    //
    //   The path to the CLI configuration file. Default is empty.
    // bundleConfig = file(../rn-cli.config.js)
    //
    //   The name of the generated asset file containing your JS bundle
    // bundleAssetName = "MyApplication.android.bundle"
    //
    //   The entry file for bundle generation. Default is 'index.android.js' or 'index.js'
    // entryFile = file("../js/MyApplication.android.js")
    //
    //   A list of extra flags to pass to the 'bundle' commands.
    //   See https://github.com/react-native-community/cli/blob/main/docs/commands.md#bundle
    // extraPackagerArgs = []

    /* Hermes Commands */
    //   The hermes compiler command to run. By default it is 'hermesc'
    // hermesCommand = "$rootDir/my-custom-hermesc/bin/hermesc"
    //
    //   The list of flags to pass to the Hermes compiler. By default is "-O", "-output-source-map"
    // hermesFlags = ["-O", "-output-source-map"]

    /* Autolinking */
    autolinkLibrariesWithApp()
}

/**
 * Set this to true in release builds to optimize the app using [R8](https://developer.android.com/topic/performance/app-optimization/enable-app-optimization).
 */
def enableMinifyInReleaseBuilds = (findProperty('android.enableMinifyInReleaseBuilds') ?: false).toBoolean()

/**
 * The preferred build flavor of JavaScriptCore (JSC)
 *
 * For example, to use the international variant, you can use:
 * `def jscFlavor = 'org.webkit:android-jsc-intl:+'`
 *
 * The international variant includes ICU i18n library and necessary data
 * allowing to use e.g. `Date.toLocaleString` and `String.localeCompare` that
 * give correct results when using with locales other than en-US. Note that
 * this variant is about 6MiB larger per architecture than default.
 */
def jscFlavor = 'io.github.react-native-community:jsc-android:2026004.+'

android {
    ndkVersion rootProject.ext.ndkVersion

    buildToolsVersion rootProject.ext.buildToolsVersion
    compileSdk rootProject.ext.compileSdkVersion

    namespace 'run.eyg.nativeapp'
    defaultConfig {
        applicationId 'run.eyg.nativeapp'
        minSdkVersion rootProject.ext.minSdkVersion
        targetSdkVersion rootProject.ext.targetSdkVersion
        versionCode 1
        versionName "0.1.0"

        buildConfigField "String", "REACT_NATIVE_RELEASE_LEVEL", "\"${findProperty('reactNativeReleaseLevel') ?: 'stable'}\""
    }
    signingConfigs {
        debug {
            storeFile file('debug.keystore')
            storePassword 'android'
            keyAlias 'androiddebugkey'
            keyPassword 'android'
        }
    }
    buildTypes {
        debug {
            signingConfig signingConfigs.debug
        }
        release {
            // Caution! In production, you need to generate your own keystore file.
            // see https://reactnative.dev/docs/signed-apk-android.
            signingConfig signingConfigs.debug
            def enableShrinkResources = findProperty('android.enableShrinkResourcesInReleaseBuilds') ?: 'false'
            shrinkResources enableShrinkResources.toBoolean()
            minifyEnabled enableMinifyInReleaseBuilds
            proguardFiles getDefaultProguardFile("proguard-android-optimize.txt"), "proguard-rules.pro"
            def enablePngCrunchInRelease = findProperty('android.enablePngCrunchInReleaseBuilds') ?: 'true'
            crunchPngs enablePngCrunchInRelease.toBoolean()
        }
    }
    packagingOptions {
        jniLibs {
            def enableLegacyPackaging = findProperty('expo.useLegacyPackaging') ?: 'false'
            useLegacyPackaging enableLegacyPackaging.toBoolean()
        }
    }
    androidResources {
        ignoreAssetsPattern '!.svn:!.git:!.ds_store:!*.scc:!CVS:!thumbs.db:!picasa.ini:!*~'
    }
}

// Apply static values from `gradle.properties` to the `android.packagingOptions`
// Accepts values in comma delimited lists, example:
// android.packagingOptions.pickFirsts=/LICENSE,**/picasa.ini
["pickFirsts", "excludes", "merges", "doNotStrip"].each { prop ->
    // Split option: 'foo,bar' -> ['foo', 'bar']
    def options = (findProperty("android.packagingOptions.$prop") ?: "").split(",");
    // Trim all elements in place.
    for (i in 0..<options.size()) options[i] = options[i].trim();
    // `[] - ""` is essentially `[""].filter(Boolean)` removing all empty strings.
    options -= ""

    if (options.length > 0) {
        println "android.packagingOptions.$prop += $options ($options.length)"
        // Ex: android.packagingOptions.pickFirsts += '**/SCCS/**'
        options.each {
            android.packagingOptions[prop] += it
        }
    }
}

dependencies {
    // The version of react-native is set by the React Native Gradle Plugin
    implementation("com.facebook.react:react-android")

    def isGifEnabled = (findProperty('expo.gif.enabled') ?: "") == "true";
    def isWebpEnabled = (findProperty('expo.webp.enabled') ?: "") == "true";
    def isWebpAnimatedEnabled = (findProperty('expo.webp.animated') ?: "") == "true";

    if (isGifEnabled) {
        // For animated gif support
        implementation("com.facebook.fresco:animated-gif:${expoLibs.versions.fresco.get()}")
    }

    if (isWebpEnabled) {
        // For webp support
        implementation("com.facebook.fresco:webpsupport:${expoLibs.versions.fresco.get()}")
        if (isWebpAnimatedEnabled) {
            // Animated webp support
            implementation("com.facebook.fresco:animated-webp:${expoLibs.versions.fresco.get()}")
        }
    }

    if (hermesEnabled.toBoolean()) {
        implementation("com.facebook.react:hermes-android")
    } else {
        implementation jscFlavor
    }
}
```

## `packages/zig_runtime/android/android/app/src/main/java/run/eyg/nativeapp/MainActivity.kt`

<!-- eyg-source: {"path":"packages/zig_runtime/android/android/app/src/main/java/run/eyg/nativeapp/MainActivity.kt","sha256":"490b14a67a82a1233f9af717a53689e2faa3c95d5d189c5f537eb526c2a00cd9","bytes":2187} -->
```text
package run.eyg.nativeapp

import android.os.Build
import android.os.Bundle

import com.facebook.react.ReactActivity
import com.facebook.react.ReactActivityDelegate
import com.facebook.react.defaults.DefaultNewArchitectureEntryPoint.fabricEnabled
import com.facebook.react.defaults.DefaultReactActivityDelegate

import expo.modules.ReactActivityDelegateWrapper

class MainActivity : ReactActivity() {
  override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
    // Set the theme to AppTheme BEFORE onCreate to support
    // coloring the background, status bar, and navigation bar.
    // This is required for expo-splash-screen.
    setTheme(R.style.AppTheme);
    super.onCreate(null)
  }

  /**
   * Returns the name of the main component registered from JavaScript. This is used to schedule
   * rendering of the component.
   */
  override fun getMainComponentName(): String = "main"

  /**
   * Returns the instance of the [ReactActivityDelegate]. We use [DefaultReactActivityDelegate]
   * which allows you to enable New Architecture with a single boolean flags [fabricEnabled]
   */
  override fun createReactActivityDelegate(): ReactActivityDelegate {
    return ReactActivityDelegateWrapper(
          this,
          BuildConfig.IS_NEW_ARCHITECTURE_ENABLED,
          object : DefaultReactActivityDelegate(
              this,
              mainComponentName,
              fabricEnabled
          ){})
  }

  /**
    * Align the back button behavior with Android S
    * where moving root activities to background instead of finishing activities.
    * @see <a href="https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/Activity#onBackPressed()">onBackPressed</a>
    */
  override fun invokeDefaultOnBackPressed() {
      if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT <= Build.VERSION_CODES.R) {
          if (!moveTaskToBack(false)) {
              // For non-root activities, use the default implementation to finish them.
              super.invokeDefaultOnBackPressed()
          }
          return
      }

      // Use the default back button implementation on Android S
      // because it's doing more than [Activity.moveTaskToBack] in fact.
      super.invokeDefaultOnBackPressed()
  }
}
```

<!-- eyg-source: {"path":"packages/zig_runtime/android/android/app/src/main/java/run/eyg/nativeapp/MainApplication.kt","sha256":"c1a82fecc757437e1dadb6b4b472a77bf4daf1ee545e0fca575c8c302e7995a9","bytes":1489} -->
```text
package run.eyg.nativeapp

import android.app.Application
import android.content.res.Configuration

import com.facebook.react.PackageList
import com.facebook.react.ReactApplication
import com.facebook.react.ReactNativeApplicationEntryPoint.loadReactNative
import com.facebook.react.ReactPackage
import com.facebook.react.ReactHost
import com.facebook.react.common.ReleaseLevel
import com.facebook.react.defaults.DefaultNewArchitectureEntryPoint

import expo.modules.ApplicationLifecycleDispatcher
import expo.modules.ExpoReactHostFactory

class MainApplication : Application(), ReactApplication {

  override val reactHost: ReactHost by lazy {
    ExpoReactHostFactory.getDefaultReactHost(
      context = applicationContext,
      packageList =
        PackageList(this).packages.apply {
          // Packages that cannot be autolinked yet can be added manually here, for example:
          // add(MyReactNativePackage())
        }
    )
  }

  override fun onCreate() {
    super.onCreate()
    DefaultNewArchitectureEntryPoint.releaseLevel = try {
      ReleaseLevel.valueOf(BuildConfig.REACT_NATIVE_RELEASE_LEVEL.uppercase())
    } catch (e: IllegalArgumentException) {
      ReleaseLevel.STABLE
    }
    loadReactNative(this)
    ApplicationLifecycleDispatcher.onApplicationCreate(this)
  }

  override fun onConfigurationChanged(newConfig: Configuration) {
    super.onConfigurationChanged(newConfig)
    ApplicationLifecycleDispatcher.onConfigurationChanged(this, newConfig)
  }
}
```

```text
newArchEnabled=true

edgeToEdgeEnabled=true

# Enable GIF support in React Native's <Image> component.
# Disable to reduce app size if you only render GIFs via expo-image.
# See https://docs.expo.dev/distribution/app-size/
expo.gif.enabled=true

expo.webp.enabled=true
# Enable animated WebP support in React Native's <Image> component.
# Disabled by default because iOS doesn't support animated WebP.
expo.webp.animated=false

# Enable network inspector
EX_DEV_CLIENT_NETWORK_INSPECTOR=true

expo.useLegacyPackaging=false

# Opt out of built-in kotlin and new DSL behavior that ships with AGP 9.
# Starting from AGP 10.x these opt outs will be removed.
android.builtInKotlin=false
android.newDsl=false

expo.inlineModules.watchedDirectories=[]
android.minSdkVersion=26
```

```text
##############################################################################
#
#   Gradle start up script for POSIX generated by Gradle.
#
#   Important for running:
#
#   (1) You need a POSIX-compliant shell to run this script. If your /bin/sh is
#       noncompliant, but you have some other compliant shell such as ksh or
#       bash, then to run this script, type that shell name before the whole
#       command line, like:
#
#           ksh Gradle
#
#       Busybox and similar reduced shells will NOT work, because this script
#       requires all of these POSIX shell features:
#         * functions;
#         * expansions «$var», «${var}», «${var:-default}», «${var+SET}»,
#           «${var#prefix}», «${var%suffix}», and «$( cmd )»;
#         * compound commands having a testable exit status, especially «case»;
#         * various built-in commands including «command», «set», and «ulimit».
#
#   Important for patching:
#
#   (2) This script targets any POSIX shell, so it avoids extensions provided
#       by Bash, Ksh, etc; in particular arrays are avoided.
#
#       The "traditional" practice of packing multiple parameters into a
#       space-separated string is a well documented source of bugs and security
#       problems, so this is (mostly) avoided, by progressively accumulating
#       options in "$@", and eventually passing that to Java.
#
#       Where the inherited environment variables (DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS,
#       and GRADLE_OPTS) rely on word-splitting, this is performed explicitly;
#       see the in-line comments for details.
#
#       There are tweaks for specific operating systems such as AIX, CygWin,
#       Darwin, MinGW, and NonStop.
#
#   (3) This script is generated from the Groovy template
#       https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/HEAD/platforms/jvm/plugins-application/src/main/resources/org/gradle/api/internal/plugins/unixStartScript.txt
#       within the Gradle project.
#
#       You can find Gradle at https://github.com/gradle/gradle/.
#
##############################################################################

# Attempt to set APP_HOME

# Resolve links: $0 may be a link
app_path=$0

# Need this for daisy-chained symlinks.
while
    APP_HOME=${app_path%"${app_path##*/}"}  # leaves a trailing /; empty if no leading path
    [ -h "$app_path" ]
do
    ls=$( ls -ld "$app_path" )
    link=${ls#*' -> '}
    case $link in             #(
      /*)   app_path=$link ;; #(
      *)    app_path=$APP_HOME$link ;;
    esac
done

# This is normally unused
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
APP_BASE_NAME=${0##*/}
# Discard cd standard output in case $CDPATH is set (https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/25036)
APP_HOME=$( cd -P "${APP_HOME:-./}" > /dev/null && printf '%s\n' "$PWD" ) || exit

# Use the maximum available, or set MAX_FD != -1 to use that value.
MAX_FD=maximum

warn () {
    echo "$*"
} >&2

die () {
    echo
    echo "$*"
    echo
    exit 1
} >&2

# OS specific support (must be 'true' or 'false').
cygwin=false
msys=false
darwin=false
nonstop=false
case "$( uname )" in                #(
  CYGWIN* )         cygwin=true  ;; #(
  Darwin* )         darwin=true  ;; #(
  MSYS* | MINGW* )  msys=true    ;; #(
  NONSTOP* )        nonstop=true ;;
esac



# Determine the Java command to use to start the JVM.
if [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] ; then
    if [ -x "$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java" ] ; then
        # IBM's JDK on AIX uses strange locations for the executables
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java
    else
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/bin/java
    fi
    if [ ! -x "$JAVACMD" ] ; then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: $JAVA_HOME

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
else
    JAVACMD=java
    if ! command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1
    then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found in your PATH.

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
fi

# Increase the maximum file descriptors if we can.
if ! "$cygwin" && ! "$darwin" && ! "$nonstop" ; then
    case $MAX_FD in #(
      max*)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -H is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        MAX_FD=$( ulimit -H -n ) ||
            warn "Could not query maximum file descriptor limit"
    esac
    case $MAX_FD in  #(
      '' | soft) :;; #(
      *)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -n is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        ulimit -n "$MAX_FD" ||
            warn "Could not set maximum file descriptor limit to $MAX_FD"
    esac
fi

# Collect all arguments for the java command, stacking in reverse order:
#   * args from the command line
#   * the main class name
#   * -classpath
#   * -D...appname settings
#   * --module-path (only if needed)
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and GRADLE_OPTS environment variables.

# For Cygwin or MSYS, switch paths to Windows format before running java
if "$cygwin" || "$msys" ; then
    APP_HOME=$( cygpath --path --mixed "$APP_HOME" )

    JAVACMD=$( cygpath --unix "$JAVACMD" )

    # Now convert the arguments - kludge to limit ourselves to /bin/sh
    for arg do
        if
            case $arg in                                #(
              -*)   false ;;                            # don't mess with options #(
              /?*)  t=${arg#/} t=/${t%%/*}              # looks like a POSIX filepath
                    [ -e "$t" ] ;;                      #(
              *)    false ;;
            esac
        then
            arg=$( cygpath --path --ignore --mixed "$arg" )
        fi

        # args, so each arg winds up back in the position where it started, but
        # possibly modified.

        # changing the positional parameters here affects neither the number of
        # iterations, nor the values presented in `arg`.
        shift                   # remove old arg
        set -- "$@" "$arg"      # push replacement arg
    done
fi


# Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS='"-Xmx64m" "-Xms64m"'

# Collect all arguments for the java command:
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and optsEnvironmentVar are not allowed to contain shell fragments,
#     and any embedded shellness will be escaped.
#   * For example: A user cannot expect ${Hostname} to be expanded, as it is an environment variable and will be
#     treated as '${Hostname}' itself on the command line.

set -- \
        "-Dorg.gradle.appname=$APP_BASE_NAME" \
        -jar "$APP_HOME/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar" \
        "$@"

# Stop when "xargs" is not available.
if ! command -v xargs >/dev/null 2>&1
then
    die "xargs is not available"
fi

# Use "xargs" to parse quoted args.
#
# With -n1 it outputs one arg per line, with the quotes and backslashes removed.
#
# In Bash we could simply go:
#
#   readarray ARGS < <( xargs -n1 <<<"$var" ) &&
#   set -- "${ARGS[@]}" "$@"
#
# but POSIX shell has neither arrays nor command substitution, so instead we
# post-process each arg (as a line of input to sed) to backslash-escape any
# character that might be a shell metacharacter, then use eval to reverse
# that process (while maintaining the separation between arguments), and wrap
# the whole thing up as a single "set" statement.
#
# This will of course break if any of these variables contains a newline or
# an unmatched quote.
#

eval "set -- $(
        printf '%s\n' "$DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS $JAVA_OPTS $GRADLE_OPTS" |
        xargs -n1 |
        sed ' s~[^-[:alnum:]+,./:=@_]~\\&~g; ' |
        tr '\n' ' '
    )" '"$@"'

exec "$JAVACMD" "$@"
```

```text
@rem limitations under the License.
@rem
@rem SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
@rem

@if "%DEBUG%"=="" @echo off
@rem ##########################################################################
@rem
@rem  Gradle startup script for Windows
@rem
@rem ##########################################################################

@rem Set local scope for the variables with windows NT shell
if "%OS%"=="Windows_NT" setlocal

set DIRNAME=%~dp0
if "%DIRNAME%"=="" set DIRNAME=.
@rem This is normally unused
set APP_BASE_NAME=%~n0
set APP_HOME=%DIRNAME%

@rem Resolve any "." and ".." in APP_HOME to make it shorter.
for %%i in ("%APP_HOME%") do set APP_HOME=%%~fi

@rem Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
set DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS="-Xmx64m" "-Xms64m"

@rem Find java.exe
if defined JAVA_HOME goto findJavaFromJavaHome

set JAVA_EXE=java.exe
%JAVA_EXE% -version >NUL 2>&1
if %ERRORLEVEL% equ 0 goto execute

echo. 1>&2
echo ERROR: JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found in your PATH. 1>&2
echo. 1>&2
echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the 1>&2
echo location of your Java installation. 1>&2

goto fail

:findJavaFromJavaHome
set JAVA_HOME=%JAVA_HOME:"=%
set JAVA_EXE=%JAVA_HOME%/bin/java.exe

if exist "%JAVA_EXE%" goto execute

echo. 1>&2
echo ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: %JAVA_HOME% 1>&2
echo. 1>&2
echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the 1>&2
echo location of your Java installation. 1>&2

goto fail

:execute
@rem Setup the command line



@rem Execute Gradle
"%JAVA_EXE%" %DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS% %JAVA_OPTS% %GRADLE_OPTS% "-Dorg.gradle.appname=%APP_BASE_NAME%" -jar "%APP_HOME%\gradle\wrapper\gradle-wrapper.jar" %*

:end
@rem End local scope for the variables with windows NT shell
if %ERRORLEVEL% equ 0 goto mainEnd

:fail
rem Set variable GRADLE_EXIT_CONSOLE if you need the _script_ return code instead of
rem the _cmd.exe /c_ return code!
set EXIT_CODE=%ERRORLEVEL%
if %EXIT_CODE% equ 0 set EXIT_CODE=1
if not ""=="%GRADLE_EXIT_CONSOLE%" exit %EXIT_CODE%
exit /b %EXIT_CODE%

:mainEnd
if "%OS%"=="Windows_NT" endlocal

:omega
```

```text
pluginManagement {
  def reactNativeGradlePlugin = new File(
    providers.exec {
      workingDir(rootDir)
      commandLine("node", "--print", "require.resolve('@react-native/gradle-plugin/package.json', { paths: [require.resolve('react-native/package.json')] })")
    }.standardOutput.asText.get().trim()
  ).getParentFile().absolutePath
  includeBuild(reactNativeGradlePlugin)
  
  def expoPluginsPath = new File(
    providers.exec {
      workingDir(rootDir)
      commandLine("node", "--print", "require.resolve('expo-modules-autolinking/package.json', { paths: [require.resolve('expo/package.json')] })")
    }.standardOutput.asText.get().trim(),
    "../android/expo-gradle-plugin"
  ).absolutePath
  includeBuild(expoPluginsPath)
}

plugins {
  id("com.facebook.react.settings")
  id("expo-autolinking-settings")
}

extensions.configure(com.facebook.react.ReactSettingsExtension) { ex ->
  if (System.getenv('EXPO_USE_COMMUNITY_AUTOLINKING') == '1') {
    ex.autolinkLibrariesFromCommand()
  } else {
    ex.autolinkLibrariesFromCommand(expoAutolinking.rnConfigCommand)
  }
}
expoAutolinking.useExpoModules()

rootProject.name = 'EYG'

expoAutolinking.useExpoVersionCatalog()

include ':app'
includeBuild(expoAutolinking.reactNativeGradlePlugin)
```

## `packages/zig_runtime/android/apk-build-blocker.txt`

<!-- eyg-source: {"path":"packages/zig_runtime/android/apk-build-blocker.txt","sha256":"48f86e47b4b0e295ca9de8d53fd2bc852239dc69c832efdda7170e3fe319ca24","bytes":896} -->
```text
APK assembly reached Android/Kotlin compilation and native module autolinking.
The final build is blocked by the managed environment HTTP destination policy:

https://repo.reactnative.dev/maven2/com/facebook/react/react-android/0.88.1/react-android-0.88.1-debug.aar

Maven Central redirects the official React Native artifact to this host. The
proxy returns HTTP 403 because repo.reactnative.dev is outside the allowlist.
Allow this host in the environment network configuration, then repeat:

cd packages/zig_runtime/android/android
ANDROID_HOME=/path/to/sdk ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug --no-daemon

Zig/JNI Android ARM64 and x86-64 libraries already cross-compile successfully.
The app's Expo prebuild, TypeScript, Android Hermes bundle, JS effects tests,
actual host JNI tests, and native C ABI differential oracle checks pass.
No APK or successful device launch is claimed in this delivery.
```

```json
  "platformNotes": [
    "SDK58 expo-widgets includes Android widgets/custom notifications despite its iOS-oriented README; layouts need the widget compiler and declared Android provider configuration.",
    "SDK58 expo-symbols implements Android Material Symbols in JavaScript/assets although its native module config lists Apple.",
    "SDK58 expo-tracking-transparency exposes Android Advertising ID; its tracking permission prompts apply to iOS.",
    "expo-updates requires a configured updates URL/runtime and signed release build for remote updates; no update service is configured by default.",

    "Registration covers package entrypoints and listed Android subpaths, not proof of every export behavior or native feature on hardware.",
    "React hooks are not imperative phone effects; call corresponding SDK functions or mount their exported components.",
    "ExpoView supports nested descriptor children; protected APIs still require Expo permission calls.",
    "eyg-widgets supplies a precompiled generic tree layout and declared EygWidget Android provider. Additional widget providers/layout code require a rebuild; runtime EYG callbacks cannot be serialized as widget worklets.",
    "Reanimated/Worklets UI-thread callbacks also require precompiled worklets; runtime EYG callbacks execute in the JavaScript host.",
    "eyg-background restores durable source entrypoints behind 16 synchronously defined TaskManager slots; each OS callback starts a fresh VM. Live continuation serialization is not implemented.",
    "Background slot identities survive forget to prevent stale delivery to another task; 16 historical names until verified resetSlots and JavaScript process restart.",
    "Synchronous dynamic callbacks use isolated pure EYG source with max10000 total VM steps, fixed4MiB allocator, 4096-byte source and64KiB input/output. Effects, references, structural equal and substring split/replace builtins are rejected.",
```

<!-- eyg-source: {"path":"packages/zig_runtime/android/modules/eyg-runtime/android/src/main/cpp/eyg_jni.c","sha256":"d3faf5f3a3d20420bf352d737fec30e93ba177c1ec28e0d63e08ab82dd8e89c0","bytes":2619} -->
```c
#include <jni.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>

extern void *eyg_android_create(void);
extern const uint8_t *eyg_android_evaluate(void *, const uint8_t *, size_t);
extern const uint8_t *eyg_android_resume(void *, const uint8_t *, size_t);
extern const uint8_t *eyg_android_pure(void *, const uint8_t *, size_t);
extern size_t eyg_android_result_len(void *);
extern void eyg_android_destroy(void *);
extern void eyg_android_cancel(void *);

JNIEXPORT jlong JNICALL Java_expo_modules_eyg_EygNative_create(JNIEnv *env, jobject self) {
  (void)env; (void)self;
  return (jlong)(intptr_t)eyg_android_create();
}

static jbyteArray evaluate(JNIEnv *env, jlong session, jbyteArray input, int resume) {
  if (!input || !session) return NULL;
  jsize length = (*env)->GetArrayLength(env, input);
  jbyte *bytes = (*env)->GetByteArrayElements(env, input, NULL);
  if (!bytes) return NULL;
  void *state = (void *)(intptr_t)session;
  const uint8_t *result = resume == 2
    ? eyg_android_pure(state, (const uint8_t *)bytes, (size_t)length)
    : resume
    ? eyg_android_resume(state, (const uint8_t *)bytes, (size_t)length)
    : eyg_android_evaluate(state, (const uint8_t *)bytes, (size_t)length);
  (*env)->ReleaseByteArrayElements(env, input, bytes, JNI_ABORT);
  size_t result_len = eyg_android_result_len(state);
  if (!result || result_len > INT32_MAX) return NULL;
  jbyteArray output = (*env)->NewByteArray(env, (jsize)result_len);
  if (output) (*env)->SetByteArrayRegion(env, output, 0, (jsize)result_len, (const jbyte *)result);
  return output;
}

JNIEXPORT jbyteArray JNICALL Java_expo_modules_eyg_EygNative_evaluate(JNIEnv *env, jobject self, jlong session, jbyteArray input) {
  (void)self; return evaluate(env, session, input, 0);
}
JNIEXPORT jbyteArray JNICALL Java_expo_modules_eyg_EygNative_resume(JNIEnv *env, jobject self, jlong session, jbyteArray input) {
  (void)self; return evaluate(env, session, input, 1);
}
JNIEXPORT jbyteArray JNICALL Java_expo_modules_eyg_EygNative_pure(JNIEnv *env, jobject self, jbyteArray input) {
  (void)self;
  void *session = eyg_android_create();
  if (!session) return NULL;
  jbyteArray result = evaluate(env, (jlong)(intptr_t)session, input, 2);
  eyg_android_destroy(session);
  return result;
}
JNIEXPORT void JNICALL Java_expo_modules_eyg_EygNative_destroy(JNIEnv *env, jobject self, jlong session) {
  (void)env; (void)self; eyg_android_destroy((void *)(intptr_t)session);
}
JNIEXPORT void JNICALL Java_expo_modules_eyg_EygNative_cancel(JNIEnv *env, jobject self, jlong session) {
  (void)env; (void)self; eyg_android_cancel((void *)(intptr_t)session);
}
```

## `packages/zig_runtime/android/modules/eyg-runtime/android/src/main/java/expo/modules/eyg/EygRuntimeModule.kt`

<!-- eyg-source: {"path":"packages/zig_runtime/android/modules/eyg-runtime/android/src/main/java/expo/modules/eyg/EygRuntimeModule.kt","sha256":"b70cbebac9a19a48b969c06dd005959e0ce7a97c52d1ac1b25385ead0c62e188","bytes":1335} -->
```text
package expo.modules.eyg
```

```text
import expo.modules.kotlin.modules.Module
import expo.modules.kotlin.modules.ModuleDefinition
import expo.modules.kotlin.functions.Coroutine
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext

/** Sessions own their Zig arena. JNI handles never cross into JavaScript. */
class EygRuntimeModule : Module() {
  private val sessions = NativeSessions(EygNative)

  override fun definition() = ModuleDefinition {
    Name("EygRuntime")
    Function("pureSync") { request: String ->
      // Isolated, data-only VM with a strict step/memory/input budget. It never
      // borrows an async session and cannot make a phone/native effect call.
      String(EygNative.pure(request.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8)), Charsets.UTF_8)
    }
    AsyncFunction("create") Coroutine {
      withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { sessions.create() }
    }
    AsyncFunction("evaluate") Coroutine { id: Int, request: String ->
      withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { sessions.call(id, request, false) }
    }
    AsyncFunction("resume") Coroutine { id: Int, reply: String ->
      withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { sessions.call(id, reply, true) }
    }
    AsyncFunction("destroy") Coroutine { id: Int ->
      withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { sessions.destroy(id) }
    }
    OnDestroy {
      sessions.close()
    }
  }

}
```

## `packages/zig_runtime/android/modules/eyg-runtime/android/src/main/java/expo/modules/eyg/NativeSessions.kt`

<!-- eyg-source: {"path":"packages/zig_runtime/android/modules/eyg-runtime/android/src/main/java/expo/modules/eyg/NativeSessions.kt","sha256":"7ea9ce6d58ecd8f8bf03cbaf077c4378cf970a54ac69902f6b493dcc7274ea34","bytes":3243} -->
```text
package expo.modules.eyg

import java.util.concurrent.Executors

internal interface NativeBackend {
  fun create(): Long
  fun evaluate(session: Long, request: ByteArray): ByteArray
  fun resume(session: Long, reply: ByteArray): ByteArray
  fun cancel(session: Long)
  fun destroy(session: Long)
}

/** Owns native pointers; only integer IDs cross the JavaScript boundary. */
internal class NativeSessions(private val native: NativeBackend) : AutoCloseable {
  private class Session(val pointer: Long) {
    val serial = Any()
    var calls = 0
    var closed = false
  }

  private val sessions = mutableMapOf<Int, Session>()
  private val ownership = Any()
  private val disposer = Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor()
  private var nextId = 1
  private var closed = false

  fun create(): Int {
    synchronized(ownership) { check(!closed) { "Zig runtime has been destroyed" } }
    val pointer = native.create()
    check(pointer != 0L) { "Unable to allocate Zig interpreter" }
    val id = synchronized(ownership) {
      if (closed) null else nextId++.also { sessions[it] = Session(pointer) }
    }
    if (id != null) return id
    // Creation runs on an IO worker. Shutdown can win without waiting for it.
    native.destroy(pointer)
    error("Zig runtime has been destroyed")
  }

  fun call(id: Int, text: String, resume: Boolean): String {
    val session = synchronized(ownership) {
      (sessions[id] ?: error("Closed Zig session")).also { it.calls++ }
    }
    try {
      synchronized(session.serial) {
        check(synchronized(ownership) { !session.closed }) { "Closed Zig session" }
        val input = text.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8)
        val output = if (resume) native.resume(session.pointer, input) else native.evaluate(session.pointer, input)
        return output.toString(Charsets.UTF_8)
      }
    } finally {
      val lastOwner = synchronized(ownership) {
        session.calls--
        session.closed && session.calls == 0
      }
      if (lastOwner) native.destroy(session.pointer)
    }
  }

  /** Called by the Expo module's IO dispatcher; a live call keeps ownership. */
  fun destroy(id: Int) {
    val idle = synchronized(ownership) {
      sessions[id]?.let { session ->
        // Holding ownership prevents the last IO worker from freeing this
        // pointer while the lock-free native cancellation flag is being set.
        if (session.calls > 0) native.cancel(session.pointer)
        sessions.remove(id)
        session.closed = true
        session.takeIf { it.calls == 0 }
      }
    }
    idle?.let { native.destroy(it.pointer) }
  }

  /** Does not join IO workers or acquire a session's evaluation lock. */
  override fun close() {
    val idle = synchronized(ownership) {
      if (closed) return
      closed = true
      val owned = sessions.values.toList()
      owned.forEach {
        if (it.calls > 0) native.cancel(it.pointer)
        it.closed = true
      }
      sessions.clear()
      owned.filter { it.calls == 0 }
    }
    // Idle arenas may be large. Free them off the lifecycle/UI thread too.
    // Active calls release their final pointer in their own IO worker.
    disposer.execute { idle.forEach { native.destroy(it.pointer) } }
    disposer.shutdown()
  }
}
```

## `packages/zig_runtime/android/scripts/benchmark-native.py`

<!-- eyg-source: {"path":"packages/zig_runtime/android/scripts/benchmark-native.py","sha256":"7c763d80f8978fe43025cae7f33723aef57090828b4f11484e32f742d3bf94e9","bytes":4505} -->
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Benchmark the C ABI on the current host; this is not a device latency claim."""
import argparse
import ctypes
import json
import statistics
import time
from pathlib import Path

def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument('library')
    p.add_argument('--iterations', type=int, default=10000)
    p.add_argument('--output', type=Path)
    p.add_argument('--budget-ms', type=float, default=10)
    p.add_argument('--pure', action='store_true', help='Also measure isolated synchronous callback creation/evaluation/destruction')
    args = p.parse_args()
    lib = ctypes.CDLL(args.library)
    lib.eyg_android_create.restype = ctypes.c_void_p
    lib.eyg_android_destroy.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p]
    lib.eyg_android_result_len.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p]
    lib.eyg_android_result_len.restype = ctypes.c_size_t
    for name in ['eyg_android_evaluate', 'eyg_android_resume'] + (['eyg_android_pure'] if args.pure else []):
        fn = getattr(lib, name)
        fn.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_size_t]
        fn.restype = ctypes.c_void_p
    session = lib.eyg_android_create()
    program = json.dumps({'source': '!int_add(20, 22)'}).encode()
    effect = json.dumps({'source': 'let n = perform Expo(20) !int_add(n, 22)'}).encode()
    reply = json.dumps({'integer': 20}).encode()
    pure_request = json.dumps({'source': '(args) -> { !int_add(args, 22) }', 'argument': {'integer': 20}, 'max_steps': 100}).encode()
    def call(fn, data):
        started = time.perf_counter_ns()
        result = fn(session, data, len(data))
        assert result
        return (time.perf_counter_ns() - started) / 1_000_000
    def pure_call(verify=False):
        started = time.perf_counter_ns()
        isolated = lib.eyg_android_create()
        assert isolated
        try:
            result = lib.eyg_android_pure(isolated, pure_request, len(pure_request))
            assert result
            if verify:
                response = json.loads(ctypes.string_at(result, lib.eyg_android_result_len(isolated)))
                assert response['status'] == 'done' and response['result'] == {'value': {'integer': 42}}
        finally:
            lib.eyg_android_destroy(isolated)
        return (time.perf_counter_ns() - started) / 1_000_000
    try:
        def verified(fn, data, expected):
            result = fn(session, data, len(data))
            assert json.loads(ctypes.string_at(result, lib.eyg_android_result_len(session))) == expected
        done = {'status': 'done', 'result': {'value': {'integer': 42}}}
        verified(lib.eyg_android_evaluate, program, done)
        verified(lib.eyg_android_evaluate, effect, {'status': 'effect', 'effect': {'label': 'Expo', 'value': {'integer': 20}}})
        verified(lib.eyg_android_resume, reply, done)
        if args.pure: pure_call(verify=True)
        for _ in range(200): call(lib.eyg_android_evaluate, program)
        evaluate, resume, pure = [], [], []
        for _ in range(args.iterations):
            evaluate.append(call(lib.eyg_android_evaluate, program))
            call(lib.eyg_android_evaluate, effect)
            resume.append(call(lib.eyg_android_resume, reply))
            if args.pure: pure.append(pure_call())
    finally:
        lib.eyg_android_destroy(session)
    def summary(values):
        values = sorted(values)
        return { 'p50_ms': statistics.median(values), 'p95_ms': values[int(len(values) * .95)], 'p99_ms': values[int(len(values) * .99)], 'max_ms': max(values) }
    report = {'target': 'host C ABI; Android device not measured', 'iterations': args.iterations,
              'results_verified_before_timing': True,
              'workload': 'parse/evaluate !int_add(20,22); external effect continuation resume',
              'evaluate': summary(evaluate), 'resume': summary(resume), 'budget_ms': args.budget_ms}
    report['passed'] = max(report['evaluate']['max_ms'], report['resume']['max_ms']) < args.budget_ms
    if args.pure:
        report['pure_sync_isolated'] = summary(pure)
        report['pure_sync_workload'] = 'fresh session, fixed-buffer pure function evaluation, result serialization and session destruction'
        report['passed'] = report['passed'] and report['pure_sync_isolated']['max_ms'] < args.budget_ms
    text = json.dumps(report, indent=2) + '\n'
    if args.output: args.output.write_text(text)
    print(text, end='')
    raise SystemExit(0 if report['passed'] else 1)

if __name__ == '__main__': main()
```

## `packages/zig_runtime/android/scripts/build-native.py`

<!-- eyg-source: {"path":"packages/zig_runtime/android/scripts/build-native.py","sha256":"5d9e915d156bfffb654589b329036ffd77ea10a79f7f697dada3cfcf2f78aa07","bytes":2230} -->
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compile Zig + JNI for the Android NDK; never download during a build."""
import argparse
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

APP = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
RUNTIME = APP.parent

def run(args):
    print(' '.join(map(str, args)), flush=True)
    subprocess.run(list(map(str, args)), check=True)

def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument('--ndk', type=Path, default=os.environ.get('ANDROID_NDK_HOME'))
    p.add_argument('--zig', default=os.environ.get('ZIG', shutil.which('zig')))
    p.add_argument('--abi', action='append', choices=['arm64-v8a', 'x86_64'])
    args = p.parse_args()
    if not args.ndk or not args.zig:
        p.error('Set ANDROID_NDK_HOME and ZIG (Zig 0.14.1), or pass --ndk and --zig')
    ndk = args.ndk.resolve()
    llvm = next((ndk / 'toolchains/llvm/prebuilt').glob('*'))
    api = 26
    work = APP / 'work/native'
    work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    jni = APP / 'modules/eyg-runtime/android/src/main'
    for abi in args.abi or ['arm64-v8a', 'x86_64']:
        arch, triple = {'arm64-v8a': ('aarch64', 'aarch64-linux-android'), 'x86_64': ('x86_64', 'x86_64-linux-android')}[abi]
        out = jni / 'jniLibs' / abi
        out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        libc = work / (abi + '.conf')
        libc.write_text('\n'.join([
            f'include_dir={llvm}/sysroot/usr/include',
            f'sys_include_dir={llvm}/sysroot/usr/include/{triple}',
            f'crt_dir={llvm}/sysroot/usr/lib/{triple}/{api}',
            'msvc_lib_dir=', 'kernel32_lib_dir=', 'gcc_dir=',
        ]) + '\n')
        run([args.zig, 'build-lib', RUNTIME / 'src/android_bridge.zig', '-dynamic', '-lc',
             '-target', f'{arch}-linux-android', '--libc', libc, '-O', 'ReleaseFast',
             '-fPIC', '-fstrip', '-z', 'max-page-size=16384', '-femit-bin=' + str(out / 'libeyg_zig.so'), '--name', 'eyg_zig'])
        run([llvm / 'bin' / f'{triple}{api}-clang', '-shared', '-fPIC', '-O3',
             jni / 'cpp/eyg_jni.c', '-L' + str(out), '-leyg_zig',
             '-Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384', '-Wl,-rpath,$ORIGIN', '-o', out / 'libeyg_jni.so'])

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```
